Kimberly,

We're seeing sustained 95th/99th tail latency spikes and an uptick in 5xx errors since 10:30 PDT across our recommendations endpoint. The real-time recommendations pipeline is timing out for ~4% of user requests; throughput is also degraded (~30% lower than steady state). This is causing dropped personalization in our checkout flow — we had multiple customer complaints this morning.

Attached: error-sample.log and throughput_report.csv (10:00-15:00 window).

We need: 1) an initial remediation plan with ETA for normalization, 2) confirmation of any SLO/SLA breach and a credit estimate, and 3) an exec-level contact because this is customer-facing and impacts our upcoming campaign.

Please escalate — Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I'm sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as SEV and have pulled the on-call team into the loop. Initial ask: can you confirm the primary affected region (us-west-2?) and whether you applied any config changes today (traffic shift, model pinning, or cache-clears)?

Immediate steps we are taking now:
- Enabling stricter routing to fallback pool to reduce latency tail for critical keys.
- Temporarily capping burst capacity on the variant that is showing the highest error rate.
- Requesting KV cache retention be extended for the session scope to reduce recompute.

We'll need additional logs to compute a precise credit. Marissa will coordinate a joint call for a live triage if that helps. I'm CC'ing Rishi for engineering context.

Attachments: request_sla_claim_form.pdf (simple form to capture impacted windows + usage metrics).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Director, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@widgetly.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production — elevated tail latency + 503 spike (impacting recommendations)

Jordan — quick status from infra: we've identified a hot path in the attention kernel for the gpt-recs-v2 variant that regresses at sequences > 512 when memory is contended; this shows as tail latency under sudden fanout. We're already rolling a targeted kernel patch to the serving runtime and standing up an isolated fallback model (gpt-recs-v2-quant) with lower memory footprint.

Requests for your team: provide the 10:00-15:00 correlation id range and any traffic spikes (bot scraping or campaign traffic) so we can correlate.

Proposed short-term mitigations (now -> +6 hours):
- Route 40% of traffic to fallback model (reduces tail but increases per-token cost by ~8%).
- Increase autoscale headroom on the isolated pool for 2 hours.

For accountability: I opened INF-4521 and will post runtime traces there. We'll calculate credits per contract section 4.2 — I'll model the credit using the outage window you provide.

—Rishi
VP, Serving Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@widgetly.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production — elevated tail latency + 503 spike (impacting recommendations)

Thanks — confirmation: affected region is us-west-2, campaign traffic spike at 10:42 produced a transient fanout (we're attaching the correlation IDs as requested). We accept the temporary routing to the fallback variant and have paused the campaign for the rest of the day.

We need a formal remediation plan and a credit proposal in writing (our procurement/legal team will require the DocuSign-ready agreement). Per our contract, Section 4.2, if availability SLO is not met we are entitled to service credits — please provide the calculation and the proposed credit amount.

Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@widgetly.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Widgetly remediation plan + credit proposal

Jordan / Team — following up with a concise remediation and credit proposal after cross-team analysis. Summary:
- Root cause: attention kernel regression under memory contention for gpt-recs-v2 (see INF-4521).
- Remediation: kernel patch rolled to 100% within 12 hours of detection; fallback pool in place; postmortem and performance regression tests scheduled.

Credit calculation (high level):
- Impact window: 2026-06-10T10:42:00Z to 2026-06-10T13:15:00Z (customer-reported window + our trace correlation).
- Affected requests: ~1.2M inference tokens (recommendations endpoint) during window.
- Contracted SLA: 99.9% availability. Downtime-equivalent for measured SLO deviation => estimated service credit = $18,250 (one-time credit applied to next invoice).

Offer: besides the credit, we propose a 60-day elevated support window (extended on-call coverage) and a complimentary technical deep-dive session with Rishi and runtime engineers. If acceptable, we'll prepare a DocuSign addendum and a public status communication.

Attachments: sla_credit_calc.xlsx, remediation_plan.docx

Please confirm and we'll convert to a DocuSign-ready statement of remedy.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
